body:
THE CONTRACT IS `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md`, committed on main. This ticket builds the WRITE half of §3: the gate (§3.6), the autonomy floor (§3.7) and execution (§3.8). The READ half — fetch, classify, verify, cache, cluster, rank, report — is ticket T-01M2DND1F5N336Q3GKXGSXKWFP and is a PREREQUISITE: it produces the verdicts and proposed actions this ticket decides whether to apply.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE LANE. Every risk in the design concentrates here. The read half writes nothing to GitHub and cannot close a live issue; this half can. Splitting them keeps the cross-model review of this code focused on the code that actually decides to act, rather than diluting it across a body parser, a cache and a ranker. Nothing in the toolkit made this split — `merge-forecast` measures inter-ticket merge pressure, not intra-ticket size (see issue #1009) — so it was a human judgment and is recorded here as one.

WHAT IS BEING BUILT.
1. The gate (spec §3.6): one-shot adversarial review per proposed action, `--input` artifact mode, one issue per artifact, `--min-confidence 0.3`, reviewer provider distinct from `providers.decider`. A refusal DEMOTES the action to a proposal; there is no fix-and-retry loop. The one-shot property is enforced in the CORE by recording the verdict against `(issue, contentHash)` and refusing a second attempt for the same revision — never by prose in the skill, which an agent under pressure routes around.
2. The autonomy floor (spec §3.7): `autonomyFloor` over the action classes `close`, `relabel`, `duplicate-link`, `comment`. Follow `packages/model-router/lib/floor.mjs` (a RAIL — read it, do not edit it): ONE validator every entry point calls, an omitted key yields the conservative default rather than a permissive one, and an unknown class is an operational error rather than a silently dropped entry. A floor widened relative to the MERGE BASE requires trust-root authorization — compare against the merge base, never the working copy, because the working copy is exactly what someone widening the floor controls.
3. Execution (spec §3.8): comment carrying full evidence and a durable marker FIRST, then the action. Never the reverse. The two writes are not atomic, so a re-run must detect its own marker for `(issue, contentHash)` and resume at the action rather than re-commenting; `scripts/ceremony-drift.mjs` (a RAIL) solved this shape and its module header explains why idempotence is the whole design constraint.
4. `.claude/skills/backlog-groom/SKILL.md`: the agentic wrapper that drives the CLI and runs the reviewer. It MUST NOT mutate GitHub directly — a single `gh issue close` in the wrapper bypasses the floor, the gate and comment-first in one call, structurally the same gap as rails-guard's un-gated Bash surface.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC14, AC15, AC17, AC18, AC24, AC25 and AC26 from `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md` §5. Each carries its own `verify:` command. Do not add or remove criteria.

NOTE ON AC6, flagged at P1 as the weakest criterion: it asserts the floor validator is reachable from the CLI and the library entry point, which is provable for today's two entry points but does not prevent a third being added later without the check. Prefer a structural assertion (every exported entry point routes through the one validator) over enumerating the two that exist today.

OUT OF SCOPE: everything in the read half (fetch, classify, verify, cache, cluster, rank, report) — that is the prerequisite ticket; filing new issues; modifying `issue-lanes`; reading issue comments as evidence.
title: backlog-groom WRITE path: the adversarial gate, the autonomy floor, and idempotent execution
